regions.name: header_and_module_prelude

VERSION (L105) must track .claude-plugin/plugin.json. _SCRIPT_PATH is the seed of the process-level ring: five regions re-exec or stat this exact path.

regions.name: state_store
regions.purpose: The per-user watch store: platform state-dir resolution, atomic + merge-on-write JSON state, an inter-process lock, the auth token, port derivation, and the repo roster.

Consumed by hub_machinery, http_hub_server, hub_bootstrap, daemon_lifecycle, and four self-test blocks. KARTA_WATCH_STATE_DIR (L144) is the seam every self-test redirects.

regions.name: engine_join
regions.purpose: Joins the engine's derived status back to binder work_item detail (_enrich) and appends archived binders to the state as merged rows (_append_archived).
regions.notes: Two pure dict transforms with no outward references. _append_archived stamps `archived: true` (L418), the flag both split_archived and the page's retention map key on.

regions.name: archived_payload_split

regions.name: current_state

But the values embed CSS custom-property names (var(--green), var(--amber-soft), …) that only exist because theme_palette_tokens defines them — a textual dependency on regions theme_palette_tokens/css that a splitter will not see in the import graph. regions.purpose: The argparse CLI and dispatch: --self-test, --print-state, --ensure, --opt-in/--opt-out, --hub, --root/--port/--key, and the ephemeral ThreadingHTTPServer loop.
regions.notes: L5464-5466 is the --print-state branch that hub_machinery._derive_repo_state re-execs as a child — the closing edge of the process-level ring. L5485-5486 sets _Handler.required_key as class state before constructing the server (a mutable-class-attribute seam, not a constructor argument). L5481 re-imports os inside the function, shadowing the module import.

cycles: TRUE SYMBOL CYCLE — hub_bootstrap (L2470-2530) <-> daemon_lifecycle (L2531-2909). Forward edge: daemon_lifecycle:run_ensure calls hub_bootstrap:_hub_port at L2776 (`port = _hub_port(ensure_state_dir(state_dir))`; _hub_port defined L2470). Back edges: hub_bootstrap:_run_hub calls daemon_lifecycle:lost_bind_race and _probe_hub at L2499 (`outcome = lost_bind_race(lambda: _probe_hub(port, token))`; defined L2852 and L2557) and daemon_lifecycle:_self_exit_watch at L2517 (defined L2893). This is the one cycle that blocks the obvious split at the L2530/L2531 banner: cutting there breaks in both directions. Cheapest break: move _hub_port (8 lines, L2470-2477) into the state_store or daemon_lifecycle side — it only reads load_state and derive_port — which leaves a single unidirectional edge hub_bootstrap -> daemon_lifecycle.

PROCESS-LEVEL RING (not an import cycle, but real) — hub_machinery -> cli_main -> current_state, closing back through cli_main -> hub_bootstrap -> http_hub_server -> hub_machinery. hub_machinery:_derive_repo_state at L1743 runs `[sys.executable, str(_SCRIPT_PATH), '--print-state']` as a child process; that lands in cli_main:main L5464-5466, which calls current_state (L553). _SCRIPT_PATH is `Path(__file__).resolve()` (L100). Consequence for any split: whichever file ends up being _SCRIPT_PATH must still accept --print-state and must still reach current_state, and spawn_detached_hub (L2701) plus _script_digest (L1809) and _self_exit_reason (L2873) pin the same path for --hub, digest skew, and mtime self-exit. Four regions therefore share an unstated contract that one file is the executable entry point.

MIRROR-CONTRACT COUPLING — app_js <-> poll_decision. poll_decision (L1014-1026) carries `# MIRROR: change together with pollDecision() in _APP_JS` at L1021; _APP_JS's pollDecision is L1086-1090 with the matching marker at L1085. selftest_poll enforces it at L5047-5049 by slicing _APP_JS from the marker to the next `\n}\n` and comparing against inspect.getsource(poll_decision). Neither region imports the other, so the import graph shows no edge — but the two cannot be separated without carrying selftest_poll with them.

MIRROR-CONTRACT COUPLING — app_js <-> feed_indicator. _feed_transition (L981-991, marker L987) vs feedTransition (L1070-1074, marker L1069). Enforced behaviourally in selftest_poll L5021-5041, which also pins FEED_OK_STATUSES == [200, 304] (L5039) — and _build_app_js ships FEED_LIVE_LABEL/FEED_PAUSED_LABEL/FEED_PAUSE_AFTER/FEED_OK_STATUSES into the page at L1581-1585, so the Python constants are the single source for both sides.

MIRROR-CONTRACT COUPLING — app_js <-> archived_payload_split. join_archived (L511-550, marker L531) vs joinArchived (L1105-1122, marker L1104). Enforced at L4394-4396 in selftest_archived by the same marker-to-brace slice plus inspect.getsource(join_archived).

SOURCE-TEXT COUPLING — selftest_etag -> http_handler_ephemeral by literal source. L4620-4621 asserts `'hmac.compare_digest' in inspect.getsource(_Handler._key_ok)` and `'if not self.required_key' in inspect.getsource(_Handler._key_ok)`. Renaming or restructuring _Handler._key_ok fails the self-test even with behaviour unchanged. Likewise selftest_poll L5073-5079 slices _APP_JS's `  mounted() {` / `  beforeUnmount() {` blocks by exact indentation and closing text, so reformatting the JS string breaks tests.

ORDERING HAZARDS (forward references, not cycles) — page_shell_helpers:_build_app_js (L1567-1587) calls _inert_json defined later at L1615; hub_bootstrap:_run_hub (L2480) calls three daemon_lifecycle functions defined 77-413 lines later; daemon_lifecycle:_self_exit_reason (L2873) takes `script_path: Path = _SCRIPT_PATH` as a DEFAULT ARGUMENT, so region 1 must be fully evaluated before this def executes, not merely before the call. Legal at runtime, but they mean physical order does not track dependency order in the back half of the file.

MISPLACED MEMBER (blocks a clean cut, though not a cycle) — _dir_snapshot (L2910-2923) sits inside the daemon-lifecycle block but is used only by selftest_runner (L5145, L5420), and its one outward reference (LOG_FILENAME, L2921) points at hub_machinery. Any split at the L2909/L2926 boundary must move it with the self-test side and carry LOG_FILENAME's definition or import.

proposal.verdict:
SPLIT — but only in one specific shape, and the strongest justification is the test suite, not the production code.

The honest case AGAINST, stated fairly: this file's whole value proposition is "one stdlib file, `uv run --script`, no install." Every new `.py` dropped beside it inherits validate_plugin.py:447's floor (`--help` must contain the literal `--self-test`, `--self-test` must exit 0), so a split is not "move code" — it is "mint N new gated CLI entry points." A split also silently narrows three real safety mechanisms that key on `_SCRIPT_PATH` alone: `_script_digest()` (hub self-retire-on-plugin-update, consumed externally at inject_karta_status.py:500), the mtime self-exit baseline (:2513), and two whole-file source scans (:3613, :4089). And ~11 external anchors point at `serve_status.py` by path or by `serve_status.<attr>`, so the module namespace stays the ABI no matter how the file is carved — nothing actually gets smaller from a caller's view.

That case loses on three facts.

1. The "single file" premise is already false. serve_status.py:96-97 does `sys.path.insert(...)` + `import karta_next` at module top; it has been a two-file program since it shipped. Two other skills already ship sibling-module imports with a pinned idiom (resolve_pack_checklist.py:42-45, serve_status.py:95-97). `uv run --script` from any cwd, both projections, the hub's bare-`sys.executable` children, and the `spec_from_file_location` probe were all proven to import siblings. "Zero-dependency" is about third-party packages and survives untouched; only the word "self-contained" moves from file to directory.

2. 46% of the file is its own test suite (lines 2910-5432, 2523 lines). That is the part with no defensible reason to live inside its subject, and it is the part that forces serialization: every binder item that adds a fixture edits the same file, which is exactly why the last delivery ran seven serial waves. The suite is a clean contiguous excision with a single entry point at main():5462 and exactly one hard break (the `globals()["_script_digest"]` patch at 3476-3481).

3. The `--self-test` floor is cheap per file, not expensive. It wants an argparse flag that runs that module's own fixtures and exits 0 — which every extracted suite already is. The floor is a feature here: it forces each new file to stay runnable and self-checking.

Two things I explicitly do NOT recommend. (a) A subdirectory (`scripts/watch/*.py`) escapes the floor entirely — the glob is one level deep — and would drop ~2500 lines of fixtures out of the pre-commit gate. That is gate evasion dressed as tidiness and it contradicts this repo's own doctrine of enforced checks over skippable prose. (b) Carving hub/http/lifecycle apart. `_HubHandler` subclasses `_Handler`, `_run_hub` drives both, and `run_ensure` probes the hub — that entanglement is genuine, the parallelism payoff is small, and the risk is not. Explicit non-goal.

One caveat that must be said out loud: the migration itself is mostly serial, because every step deletes from serve_status.py. The parallelism is a payoff for FUTURE binders, not for this one. Anyone selling this refactor as "it will deliver in two waves" is wrong.
proposal.layout:
Flat sibling modules in `skills/karta-status/scripts/`, alongside `serve_status.py` and `karta_next.py`. No package, no subdirectory, no `__init__.py`.

Why the tooling forces this, not taste:

- `validate_plugin.py:447` globs `SKILLS.glob("*/scripts/*.py")` — one level, non-recursive. Flat siblings are gated; anything under `scripts/<subdir>/` is provably exempt (verified: `skills/*/scripts/*/*.py` matches nothing today, and a scratch-copy file moved into `scripts/watch/` flipped a hard FAIL to PASS with no other change). Choosing the subdirectory means choosing to un-gate the fixtures.
- There is not one `__init__.py` anywhere in the repo. A package would be first-of-its-kind with no precedent, no generator support, and no benefit — sibling imports already work from every invocation path in the codebase.
- Two pinned precedents exist for exactly this shape: `skills/karta-kaizen/scripts/resolve_pack_checklist.py:42-45` and `serve_status.py:95-97`. Copy the idiom verbatim, including the comment stating it is cwd-independent and that the imported module is import-safe.
- `sync_codex_skills.py` builds both projections with `sd.rglob("*")` and `mkdir(parents=True)`, so new flat files auto-mirror into `.agents/skills/` and `plugins/karta/skills/` with no manifest edit. `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` enumerates skill directories, never files.
- `serve_status.py` keeps its exact path and filename and remains the sole entry point. Six external anchors hardcode it (SKILL.md x3 installs, docs/how-to/karta-watch.md x3 commands, karta_next.py:234, inject_karta_status.py:70 plus its :361 `endswith("serve_status.py")` assertion, sec probe :98, dark probe :140-141). Code moves OUT of it; the file never moves.

Naming convention: `watch_<domain>.py` for production leaves, `watch_<domain>_selftest.py` for suites. The `watch_` prefix keeps the two entry-point names (`serve_status`, `karta_next`) visually distinct from internals in a flat directory, and `_selftest` makes the test set greppable and gives a future validator rule something to key on.

serve_status.py becomes: the process ring (`_SCRIPT_PATH`, identity, digest, lifecycle), the HTTP/hub server, the engine join, `main()`, an explicit re-export block that IS the module ABI, and a ~70-line self-test aggregator that owns the isolation seam and lazily imports the six suites.

risks: HUB SKEW GOES BLIND (highest severity, and the reason Step 0 exists). `_script_digest()` (serve_status.py:1809) is sha256 of `_SCRIPT_PATH` bytes only, and it is the value a running hub compares against to retire itself on a plugin update — consumed externally at hooks/scripts/inject_karta_status.py:500 and driven by `expected = _script_digest()` at :2772. Move any logic to a sibling without widening it and editing that sibling no longer changes the digest: a stale hub keeps serving old code across an upgrade, silently. The same applies to the self-exit mtime baseline at :2513. Mitigation: `_module_files()` in Step 0, plus the fixture asserting the list equals the set of siblings serve_status imports, so a forgotten file is a hard failure, not a silent narrowing. Second-order: the hub suite recomputes the expected digest independently at 3472 — miss that line and /identity disagrees with its own test.

THE ONE HARD BREAK: `globals()['_script_digest'] = lambda: 'tampered-post-boot'` at serve_status.py:3476-3481 is the only use of `globals()` in the entire file. In a separate test module `globals()` is that module's namespace, so `_identity_snapshot` — which resolves `_script_digest` through serve_status's globals — would never see the tampered function and the 'identity is a startup snapshot, not a re-read' check would pass VACUOUSLY. A vacuously green check is worse than a red one because nobody investigates it. Must become setattr on the imported module object, restored in `finally`, with an added positive assertion that the patch took effect before /identity is re-queried.

SOURCE-SCAN NARROWING. Three invariants read `_SCRIPT_PATH.read_text()` and would silently cover only the shrunken file after a split: the no-`--bind`/`--host`/`--interface` flag scan (3613-3631), the no-pidfile scan (4089-4100), and `src.count('_store_' + 'lock(') == 2`. The last one BREAKS OUTRIGHT if the store moves out; the other two go blind, which is worse — a future edit could reintroduce a bind-to-all-interfaces flag in watch_page.py unpoliced. Mitigation: read the concatenation of `_module_files()`, which preserves today's meaning exactly (store-lock stays 2: def at 235 + use at 282; the loopback literal stays >= 2). The split-literal trick that stops the checks self-matching still works because the test modules also spell them split.

MODULE ABI BREAK. Three independent consumers reach into serve_status by attribute: karta_next.py (ensure_state_dir, _hub_port, get_token, _probe_hub, ENSURE_FAILURE_FILENAME, _SCRIPT_PATH, upsert_repo, _record_ensure_failure, PORT_BASE, PORT_SPAN, record_port), inject_karta_status.py (upsert_repo, get_token, _script_digest, record_port, _record_ensure_failure, ensure_state_dir, ENSURE_FAILURE_FILENAME), and benchmarks/probes/dark-status-surface-probes.py (`serve_status._STATE_META`, imported with a bare `python -c` at cwd=scripts, FAIL-LOUD on ImportError, with four grading anchors in benchmarks/fixtures/stranded-states/expected.json pinning its badge words). `from watch_store import *` will NOT carry underscore-prefixed names — the re-exports must be explicit, name by name, and the Step 0 `_PUBLIC_ABI` fixture must list all 13.

CODEX PROJECTION DRIFT. Every new file lands three times: skills/, .agents/skills/, plugins/karta/skills/. The generator rglobs and creates parents, so nothing needs a manifest edit — but `sync_codex_skills.py` must be RUN and all three copies committed together, or validate_plugin fails twice ('missing from .agents/skills mirror' and 'missing from Codex install projection'), and a leftover projection reports 'orphaned (no canonical source)'. Executable bits are compared per file too. Expect roughly 3x the file churn in every commit. Also note orphan cleanup only unlinks files — an emptied projected directory lingers (harmless for git and --check, but not self-healing).

THE --self-test FLOOR IS A PER-FILE TAX AND A RUNTIME MULTIPLIER. validate_plugin.py:447 runs `--help` (substring-matching the literal `--self-test`) then `--self-test` on every one of the 8 new flat files, with a 120s timeout each. Two consequences: (a) no file may do heavy or blocking work at import time — the `--help` probe executes each module as __main__, so entry points must stay behind argparse/`if __name__`; (b) validate_plugin's wall time roughly doubles, because the hub and lifecycle suites bind loopback sockets and spawn detached processes and now run once standalone plus once via the aggregator. Hard rule to keep it at 2x and not 8x: a test module's `--self-test` runs ONLY its own checks and never calls back into serve_status's aggregator.

COLD-PATH IMPORT REGRESSION. karta_next.py:1029-1031 and inject_karta_status.py:436 both assert, in a fresh process, that a non-opted repo never pulls serve_status into sys.modules — and the hub spawns a `--print-state` child per repo on every derivation. Importing any `*_selftest` module at serve_status top level would add ~2500 lines of parse cost to every one of those children and could perturb the cold-path assertions. The six suite imports must live strictly inside the `--self-test` branch of `main()`, pinned by the new fixture.

IN-FLIGHT BINDER COLLISION. .karta/binders/watch-redesign.json is planned against the monolith: its binder-level oracle and all 7 item oracles run `serve_status.py --self-test && validate_plugin.py --self-test`, every item's `touches` lists serve_status.py plus both mirrors, and :281 cites 'serve_status.py:3604-3733' as a migration scope. Landing this split mid-flight leaves those touches lists under-declaring the new files, which is exactly the collision-detection input karta relies on. Either land the split before that binder starts building, or replan it after — do not interleave. (:301 also names a not-yet-existing anchor, skills/karta-status/scripts/selftest_behaviours.txt, whose relationship to this split needs a decision.)

CHILD-SPAWN AND PEP-723 SURFACE. The hub spawns `[sys.executable, str(_SCRIPT_PATH), '--print-state']` (1743) and `--hub --port N` (2701) with the BARE interpreter, never `uv run --script`, and karta_next.py:263 and inject_karta_status.py:362 do the same. So third-party dependencies stay banned in every new module regardless of what a PEP-723 block says — only `dependencies = []` survives. Sibling imports themselves are proven safe on all four paths (direct uv run from any cwd, both projections, the bare-interpreter children, and the `spec_from_file_location` probe) because serve_status.py:96 puts the script dir on sys.path for the whole process. But a module that is itself an entry point needs its OWN insert: karta_next.py has none at top level today (only the lazy one in `_load_watch`), so each new directly-invoked sibling must carry the pinned idiom.

SOURCE-INTROSPECTION FALSE ALARMS. Four introspection sites cross the new boundary: `inspect.getsource(join_archived)` vs `_APP_JS.index('// MIRROR: change together with join_archived()')` (4394-4396), the same shape for `poll_decision` (5047-5049), the mounted()/beforeUnmount() block extraction (5077-5079), and `inspect.getsource(_Handler._key_ok)` (4620-4621). All four are object-bound and survive the move unchanged — but the marker STRINGS at serve_status.py:531 and :1021 are themselves asserted verbatim by those comparisons, so the Step 5 prose sweep must not reword them, only the surrounding comment text. If _APP_JS and join_archived end up in different modules (page vs serve_status), the mirror comparison spans two files and its failure message should name both.

ENVIRONMENTAL FLAKES ON THIS HOST WILL BE MISREAD AS SPLIT BUGS. Two are already documented from the investigation: (a) `serve_status.py --ensure` exits 139 (SIGSEGV) under bare python3 3.13.5 while being fully green under `uv run`, which cascades into inject_karta_status.py and karta_next.py hub e2e cases; (b) intermittent, non-reproducible validator subprocess flakes falsely reporting scripts as not exposing --self-test. Every gate above must be run under `uv run`, and a red gate must be re-run once before being treated as a real regression. Also: running the validator has real side effects — it touches ~/.local/state/karta and can leave a `serve_status.py --hub --port 8765` process running against the real repo.

SEMANTIC DRIFT IN WHAT THE HUB CONSIDERS 'ITSELF'. Once `_module_files()` exists, someone will ask whether karta_next.py belongs in it — it is the derivation engine, a plugin update changes it, and it arguably should retire a stale hub too. Today it does NOT participate in the digest. Adding it is defensible but it is a behavior change to make deliberately with its own item, not a side effect of a refactor. Keep the pinned list to serve_status + the new siblings unless someone decides otherwise on purpose.

FILE COUNT AS ITS OWN COST. This ends at 10 files in one flat directory (~5715 total lines, about 200 MORE than today once per-file headers, argparse blocks and imports are counted). The line total goes UP; only the per-file maximum goes down, from 5504 to ~1620. Anyone measuring success by total lines will read this as a regression. The metric that matters is: how many binder items can edit disjoint files, and whether the test for a thing lives outside the thing.
open_questions: Are the two whole-file source scans (3613, 4089) INTENDED to police test code as well as production code? Their comments say 'appears nowhere in this script's source', which today means the whole 5504-line file including fixtures. The proposal preserves that by scanning the concatenation of `_module_files()`, but if the intent was only ever to police shipped behavior, the test modules should be excluded — and that changes what `_module_files()` means for the digest too. Someone who knows the original intent should decide, not infer.

Should the `--self-test` floor grow a rule for `*_selftest.py` files, so the suites are not run twice per validate_plugin (once standalone, once via the aggregator)? That is a validator edit and therefore a doctrine call: the floor's value is that every gated file is independently runnable, which the standalone run is exactly what proves. Recommend leaving the floor alone and accepting ~2x wall time, but the alternative deserves an explicit decision rather than a silent acceptance.

Should karta_next.py join `_module_files()` (and therefore the hub identity digest and the source scans)? It is the derivation engine, it ships in the same plugin update, and a hub running against a stale karta_next is the same class of problem the digest exists to catch. Today it is outside. Changing that is a real behavior change and belongs in its own item.

Sequencing against .karta/binders/watch-redesign.json — land the split first and replan the redesign binder against the new file set, or finish the redesign on the monolith and split after? Both are defensible; interleaving is not, because that binder's `touches` lists and its :281 line-range citation are written against the single file.

Does `skills/karta-status/scripts/selftest_behaviours.txt` (named at watch-redesign.json:301 as a validate_plugin-read anchor, absent from disk, with no code reading it yet) belong to this split or to that binder? If it is meant to be a checked inventory of fixture behaviors, this split is the moment it would be populated — or the moment it becomes six files instead of one.

Do any consumer repos outside this checkout (parchmark, gringotts) pin serve_status.py internals in their own tooling? Only this repo was searched. The re-export block covers attribute access, but a consumer that greps the file or cites line numbers would not be covered.

Is `watch_` the right prefix, given the skill is named karta-status and the product surface is 'Karta Watch'? The prefix keeps the two entry-point filenames visually distinct in a flat directory, but `status_` would match the skill name. Cosmetic, worth settling once before eight files carry it.
